    Raw schema¶

    The structure of a configuration as JSON, from the same field lists the parser reads: each object's fields with their descriptions, units, defaults and ranges, and each choice's alternatives. terraingen.config_schema() and terraingen schema give it too.

    • schema.json: this document.
    • catalog.json: every type with its defaults, as terraingen.config_catalog() gives it.
    schema.json 
    {
  "schema_version": 1,
  "root": {
    "kind": "object",
    "fields": [
      {
        "name": "schema_version",
        "description": "Version of the configuration format, which this library reads. Required.",
        "unit": "",
        "schema": {
          "kind": "integer",
          "fixed": true
        },
        "default": 1,
        "required": true
      },
      {
        "name": "body",
        "description": "What the terrain lies on: a plane in meters, or a whole body (a sphere, ellipsoid or shape model) in longitude and latitude degrees.",
        "unit": "",
        "schema": {
          "kind": "ref",
          "ref": "d0"
        },
        "default": {
          "type": "plane"
        }
      },
      {
        "name": "source",
        "description": "Where the heights come from: a GeoTIFF, a chain of sources or synthetic noise, with its upsampling; unset is fBm noise 400 m in wavelength and 12 m in amplitude at the datum.",
        "unit": "",
        "schema": {
          "kind": "optional",
          "of": {
            "kind": "ref",
            "ref": "d1"
          },
          "default": {
            "type": "raster",
            "path": "",
            "band": 0,
            "scale": null,
            "offset_m": null,
            "crop": null,
            "effective_pixel_size_m": null,
            "upsampling": "cubic"
          }
        },
        "default": null
      },
      {
        "name": "layers",
        "description": "Relief and features added to the source's heights, applied in order: noise, craters, boulders and more.",
        "unit": "",
        "schema": {
          "kind": "array",
          "of": {
            "kind": "ref",
            "ref": "d6"
          },
          "default": {
            "type": "noise",
            "stack": [
              {
                "enabled": true,
                "basis": "perlin",
                "fractal": "fbm",
                "blend": "add",
                "seed": 0,
                "wavelength_m": 1000.0,
                "amplitude_m": null,
                "octaves": 8,
                "lacunarity": 2.0,
                "gain": 0.5,
                "hurst": null,
                "offset": 1.0,
                "warp_amplitude_m": 0.0,
                "warp_wavelength_m": 500.0
              }
            ],
            "estimate_from_source": false,
            "source_resolves_px": null
          }
        },
        "default": []
      },
      {
        "name": "outputs",
        "description": "What to produce, at what resolution and where, each over its own extent or the whole body: heightmaps, crater and boulder lists, boulder models, albedo, meshes and reports. Each is returned, and written to its path when it has one.",
        "unit": "",
        "schema": {
          "kind": "array",
          "of": {
            "kind": "ref",
            "ref": "d52"
          },
          "default": {
            "type": "heightmap",
            "path": "",
            "pixel_size_m": null,
            "extent_m": null,
            "extent_deg": null,
            "compression": "lzw",
            "tile_size_px": 256
          }
        },
        "default": []
      },
      {
        "name": "albedo",
        "description": "The terrain's albedo: a source and the layers that change it, written by albedo outputs; none when unset.",
        "unit": "",
        "schema": {
          "kind": "optional",
          "of": {
            "kind": "ref",
            "ref": "d54"
          },
          "default": {
            "source": {
              "type": "synthetic",
              "rgb": false,
              "hue_deg": 0.0,
              "saturation": 0.0,
              "value": 0.11,
              "hue_noise_deg": [],
              "saturation_noise": [],
              "value_noise": []
            },
            "layers": []
          }
        },
        "default": null
      },
      {
        "name": "materials",
        "description": "The material map: soil, sand, dust, bedrock and rock shares, and their Hapke parameters, written by materials and photometry outputs; none when unset.",
        "unit": "",
        "schema": {
          "kind": "optional",
          "of": {
            "kind": "ref",
            "ref": "d68"
          },
          "default": {
            "exposure": {
              "reach_m": 12.0,
              "rise_soil": 0.01,
              "rise_boulder": 0.035,
              "slope_soil": 0.2,
              "slope_boulder": 0.4,
              "floor_cover": 0.0,
              "floor_patch_m": 60.0,
              "seed": 0
            },
            "dust_cover": 0.0,
            "dust_patch_m": 50.0,
            "seed": 0,
            "photometry": {
              "reference": "none",
              "soil": null,
              "sand": null,
              "dust": null,
              "bedrock": null,
              "rock": null
            }
          }
        },
        "default": null
      }
    ]
  },
  "definitions": {
    "d0": {
      "kind": "choice",
      "alternatives": [
        {
          "type": "plane",
          "description": "A flat projected frame in meters, for local sites.",
          "fields": [],
          "default": {
            "type": "plane"
          }
        },
        {
          "type": "sphere",
          "description": "A whole body such as a planet or moon: positions in longitude and latitude (degrees) and features generated over the whole body.",
          "fields": [
            {
              "name": "radius_m",
              "description": "Radius of the body's datum sphere, in meters. Must be positive. Required.",
              "unit": "m",
              "schema": {
                "kind": "number"
              },
              "default": 0.0,
              "minimum": 0.0,
              "exclusive_minimum": true,
              "required": true
            }
          ],
          "default": {
            "type": "sphere",
            "radius_m": 0.0
          }
        },
        {
          "type": "ellipsoid",
          "description": "A whole body shaped as a triaxial ellipsoid, such as an elongated moon or asteroid: planetocentric longitude and latitude (degrees), heights along the direction from the center, and features generated over the whole body.",
          "fields": [
            {
              "name": "radii_m",
              "description": "Semi-axes a, b and c of the datum ellipsoid in meters, along x (longitude 0), y (longitude 90) and z (the north pole). Holds exactly 3 items. Each must be positive. Required.",
              "unit": "m",
              "schema": {
                "kind": "array",
                "of": {
                  "kind": "number"
                },
                "default": 0.0
              },
              "default": [],
              "minimum": 0.0,
              "exclusive_minimum": true,
              "min_length": 3,
              "max_length": 3,
              "required": true
            }
          ],
          "default": {
            "type": "ellipsoid",
            "radii_m": []
          }
        },
        {
          "type": "shape_model",
          "description": "A whole star-shaped body such as an asteroid from a shape model, resampled along rays from its origin; heights are radial, in longitude and latitude degrees.",
          "fields": [
            {
              "name": "path",
              "description": "Shape model in body-fixed coordinates around its origin: a Gaskell ICQ model (.icq) or a closed mesh (.obj, .gltf, .glb or .stl); relative paths resolve against the configuration's folder. Required.",
              "unit": "",
              "schema": {
                "kind": "string"
              },
              "default": "",
              "required": true
            },
            {
              "name": "q",
              "description": "Intervals per cube face edge of the radial grid the model is resampled on; unset keeps an ICQ model's own Q and uses 256 for a mesh. Must be from 1 to 4096.",
              "unit": "",
              "schema": {
                "kind": "optional",
                "of": {
                  "kind": "integer",
                  "minimum": 0
                },
                "default": 0
              },
              "default": null,
              "minimum": 1.0,
              "exclusive_minimum": false,
              "maximum": 4096.0,
              "exclusive_maximum": false
            },
            {
              "name": "meters_per_unit",
              "description": "Meters per unit of the file's coordinates; unset is 1000 for an ICQ model, whose coordinates are kilometers, and 1 for a mesh. Must be positive.",
              "unit": "m/unit",
              "schema": {
                "kind": "optional",
                "of": {
                  "kind": "number"
                },
                "default": 0.0
              },
              "default": null,
              "minimum": 0.0,
              "exclusive_minimum": true
            }
          ],
          "default": {
            "type": "shape_model",
            "path": "",
            "q": null,
            "meters_per_unit": null
          }
        }
      ]
    },
    "d2": {
      "kind": "object",
      "fields": [
        {
          "name": "min_x",
          "description": "Lower edge along x.",
          "unit": "",
          "schema": {
            "kind": "number"
          },
          "default": 0.0
        },
        {
          "name": "min_y",
          "description": "Lower edge along y.",
          "unit": "",
          "schema": {
            "kind": "number"
          },
          "default": 0.0
        },
        {
          "name": "max_x",
          "description": "Upper edge along x; above min_x.",
          "unit": "",
          "schema": {
            "kind": "number"
          },
          "default": 0.0
        },
        {
          "name": "max_y",
          "description": "Upper edge along y; above min_y.",
          "unit": "",
          "schema": {
            "kind": "number"
          },
          "default": 0.0
        }
      ]
    },
    "d3": {
      "kind": "choice",
      "alternatives": [
        {
          "type": "nearest",
          "description": "The value of the nearest cell center: blocky, but never mixes values.",
          "fields": [],
          "default": "nearest"
        },
        {
          "type": "bilinear",
          "description": "Linear in each axis over the four surrounding cells.",
          "fields": [],
          "default": "bilinear"
        },
        {
          "type": "cubic",
          "description": "Keys cubic convolution (a = -0.5) over the sixteen surrounding cells: smooth, for upscaling DEMs.",
          "fields": [],
          "default": "cubic"
        },
        {
          "type": "catmull_rom",
          "description": "Another name for cubic: the Catmull-Rom spline is the same kernel.",
          "fields": [],
          "default": "catmull_rom"
        },
        {
          "type": "lanczos3",
          "description": "The three-lobe Lanczos kernel over the 36 surrounding cells: sharper than cubic, with slight ringing at steps.",
          "fields": [],
          "default": "lanczos3"
        },
        {
          "type": "cubic_bspline",
          "description": "The cubic B-spline over the sixteen surrounding cells: the smoothest, but it smooths the cells themselves.",
          "fields": [],
          "default": "cubic_bspline"
        },
        {
          "type": "diamond_square",
          "description": "Random midpoint displacement: each level halves the node spacing down to the sample spacing, adding fractal detail without changing the posts.",
          "fields": [
            {
              "name": "fractal_dimension",
              "description": "Fractal dimension, 2 smooth and 3 rough: each square or diamond step scales the displacement by 2^-((3 - F) / 2). Unset estimates it from the median height differences of the posts at lags of 1 to 8 posts. Must be from 2 to 3.",
              "unit": "",
              "schema": {
                "kind": "optional",
                "of": {
                  "kind": "number"
                },
                "default": 0.0
              },
              "default": null,
              "minimum": 2.0,
              "exclusive_minimum": false,
              "maximum": 3.0,
              "exclusive_maximum": false
            },
            {
              "name": "scale_m",
              "description": "Displacement standard deviation in meters at the posts' last step; unset estimates it per fit_window_px window. Must not be negative.",
              "unit": "m",
              "schema": {
                "kind": "optional",
                "of": {
                  "kind": "number"
                },
                "default": 0.0
              },
              "default": null,
              "minimum": 0.0,
              "exclusive_minimum": false
            },
            {
              "name": "fit_window_px",
              "description": "Side in posts of the overlapping windows, centered every half side, that an unset scale_m is fitted over; each node's scale is bilinear between the windows around it. 0 fits one scale to a sample of the posts; else at least 4. Must be from 0 to 1024 px.",
              "unit": "px",
              "schema": {
                "kind": "integer",
                "minimum": 0
              },
              "default": 32,
              "minimum": 0.0,
              "exclusive_minimum": false,
              "maximum": 1024.0,
              "exclusive_maximum": false
            },
            {
              "name": "interp",
              "description": "How new nodes are filled from the coarser ones and samples read between the finest nodes.",
              "unit": "",
              "schema": {
                "kind": "enum",
                "choices": [
                  "bilinear",
                  "catmull_rom"
                ],
                "descriptions": [
                  "Square nodes the mean of their four corners, diamond nodes the mean of their four neighbors, samples bilinear between nodes.",
                  "Catmull-Rom splines over four nodes along each axis, as the VIPER terrain expansion does: smoother, with fewer lattice creases."
                ]
              },
              "default": "bilinear"
            },
            {
              "name": "min_pixel_size_m",
              "description": "Finest node spacing in meters the posts are refined to; 0 refines down to the sample spacing. Must not be negative.",
              "unit": "m",
              "schema": {
                "kind": "number"
              },
              "default": 0.0,
              "minimum": 0.0,
              "exclusive_minimum": false
            },
            {
              "name": "seed",
              "description": "Seed of the displacements.",
              "unit": "",
              "schema": {
                "kind": "integer",
                "minimum": 0
              },
              "default": 1
            }
          ],
          "default": {
            "type": "diamond_square",
            "fractal_dimension": null,
            "scale_m": null,
            "fit_window_px": 32,
            "interp": "bilinear",
            "min_pixel_size_m": 0.0,
            "seed": 1
          }
        }
      ],
      "named": true
    },
    "d4": {
      "kind": "object",
      "fields": [
        {
          "name": "mode",
          "description": "How each source meets the gaps of those before it: none switches outright, feather fades the edge's height difference out across the gap, height shifts the later source to meet the earlier one's heights (C0) and slope to meet its heights and slopes (C1). The match is solved on the posts of the source before each gap.",
          "unit": "",
          "schema": {
            "kind": "enum",
            "choices": [
              "none",
              "feather",
              "height",
              "slope"
            ],
            "descriptions": [
              "Each cell takes the first source with data, unchanged: a step where a gap begins.",
              "Adds the height difference at the nearest edge post to the later source, fading it to 0 across width_m of the gap: the cheapest, without a solve.",
              "Shifts the later source by the edge's height difference spread smoothly into the gap, fading out over decay_length_m beyond an open edge: heights meet (C0), keeping the later source's relief.",
              "As height, with a biharmonic spread that matches slopes at the edge as well (C1)."
            ]
          },
          "default": "none"
        },
        {
          "name": "width_m",
          "description": "Width in meters of the band inside a gap over which feather fades the height difference at the edge to 0. Must be positive.",
          "unit": "m",
          "schema": {
            "kind": "number"
          },
          "default": 50.0,
          "minimum": 0.0,
          "exclusive_minimum": true
        },
        {
          "name": "decay_length_m",
          "description": "Length in meters over which height and slope fade the shift out where a gap is open, beyond a source's edge; it is 0 from three decay lengths on. A hole much narrower than it takes the whole shift. Must be positive.",
          "unit": "m",
          "schema": {
            "kind": "number"
          },
          "default": 50.0,
          "minimum": 0.0,
          "exclusive_minimum": true
        }
      ]
    },
    "d5": {
      "kind": "object",
      "fields": [
        {
          "name": "enabled",
          "description": "Includes this layer in the stack; disabled layers are skipped.",
          "unit": "",
          "schema": {
            "kind": "boolean"
          },
          "default": true
        },
        {
          "name": "basis",
          "description": "Single-octave noise the fractal is built from.",
          "unit": "",
          "schema": {
            "kind": "enum",
            "choices": [
              "perlin",
              "simplex",
              "value",
              "worley_f1",
              "worley_f2",
              "worley_f2_minus_f1",
              "voronoi"
            ],
            "descriptions": [
              "Improved Perlin gradient noise: smooth, general-purpose relief.",
              "Simplex gradient noise: smooth relief, an alternative to Perlin.",
              "Value noise: random values interpolated over a lattice; blockier than gradient noise.",
              "Cellular noise from the distance to the nearest feature point: cones and basins.",
              "Cellular noise from the distance to the second-nearest feature point.",
              "Cellular noise F2 - F1: ridges along cell borders, like cracked ground.",
              "Voronoi cells, each at one random height: flat polygonal plateaus and terraces."
            ]
          },
          "default": "perlin"
        },
        {
          "name": "fractal",
          "description": "How the octaves of the basis noise are combined.",
          "unit": "",
          "schema": {
            "kind": "enum",
            "choices": [
              "fbm",
              "ridged",
              "billow",
              "hybrid_multifractal"
            ],
            "descriptions": [
              "Fractional Brownian motion: a weighted sum of octaves, the general-purpose choice.",
              "Ridged multifractal: sharp crests from inverted absolute noise, like eroded ridges.",
              "Sum of absolute-value octaves: rounded, puffy forms.",
              "Hybrid multifractal: smooth lowlands and rough highlands."
            ]
          },
          "default": "fbm"
        },
        {
          "name": "blend",
          "description": "How this layer combines with the height of the layers before it; the first enabled layer sets the height instead.",
          "unit": "",
          "schema": {
            "kind": "enum",
            "choices": [
              "add",
              "max",
              "min",
              "mask"
            ],
            "descriptions": [
              "Adds the layer to the height so far.",
              "Keeps the higher of the height so far and the layer.",
              "Keeps the lower of the height so far and the layer.",
              "Multiplies the height so far by (layer / amplitude + 1) / 2, so the layer modulates roughness by region."
            ]
          },
          "default": "add"
        },
        {
          "name": "seed",
          "description": "Seed of the noise; changing it gives a different pattern of the same character.",
          "unit": "",
          "schema": {
            "kind": "integer",
            "minimum": 0
          },
          "default": 0
        },
        {
          "name": "wavelength_m",
          "description": "Wavelength of the first, broadest octave, in meters; sets the size of the largest features. Must be positive.",
          "unit": "m",
          "schema": {
            "kind": "number"
          },
          "default": 1000.0,
          "minimum": 0.0,
          "exclusive_minimum": true
        },
        {
          "name": "amplitude_m",
          "description": "Largest height of the layer above or below 0, in meters; unset is 0.1 times the wavelength, near the lunar highland median slope at any wavelength.",
          "unit": "m",
          "schema": {
            "kind": "optional",
            "of": {
              "kind": "number"
            },
            "default": 0.0
          },
          "default": null
        },
        {
          "name": "octaves",
          "description": "Number of octaves; each one adds detail at a shorter wavelength. Must be from 1 to 32.",
          "unit": "",
          "schema": {
            "kind": "integer"
          },
          "default": 8,
          "minimum": 1.0,
          "exclusive_minimum": false,
          "maximum": 32.0,
          "exclusive_maximum": false
        },
        {
          "name": "lacunarity",
          "description": "Frequency ratio between successive octaves. Must be above 1.",
          "unit": "",
          "schema": {
            "kind": "number"
          },
          "default": 2.0,
          "minimum": 1.0,
          "exclusive_minimum": true
        },
        {
          "name": "gain",
          "description": "Weight ratio between successive octaves; higher values give rougher terrain. Unused when the Hurst exponent is set. Must be positive.",
          "unit": "",
          "schema": {
            "kind": "number"
          },
          "default": 0.5,
          "minimum": 0.0,
          "exclusive_minimum": true
        },
        {
          "name": "hurst",
          "description": "Hurst exponent that sets the octave gain to lacunarity^-hurst: near 1 is smooth, lower is rougher at short baselines. Unset uses the gain.",
          "unit": "",
          "schema": {
            "kind": "optional",
            "of": {
              "kind": "number"
            },
            "default": 0.0
          },
          "default": null
        },
        {
          "name": "offset",
          "description": "Ridge offset of the ridged and hybrid multifractal types. Must be positive.",
          "unit": "",
          "schema": {
            "kind": "number"
          },
          "default": 1.0,
          "minimum": 0.0,
          "exclusive_minimum": true
        },
        {
          "name": "warp_amplitude_m",
          "description": "Domain warp displacement in meters, which bends the noise into swirled shapes; 0 disables warping. Must not be negative.",
          "unit": "m",
          "schema": {
            "kind": "number"
          },
          "default": 0.0,
          "minimum": 0.0,
          "exclusive_minimum": false
        },
        {
          "name": "warp_wavelength_m",
          "description": "Wavelength of the warp field, in meters. Must be positive.",
          "unit": "m",
          "schema": {
            "kind": "number"
          },
          "default": 500.0,
          "minimum": 0.0,
          "exclusive_minimum": true
        }
      ]
    },
    "d1": {
      "kind": "choice",
      "alternatives": [
        {
          "type": "raster",
          "description": "A heightmap read from a GeoTIFF in its own projected coordinates, its cells upsampled to finer spacings, to add relief to a real DEM.",
          "fields": [
            {
              "name": "path",
              "description": "GeoTIFF to read the heights from; relative paths resolve against the configuration's folder. Required.",
              "unit": "",
              "schema": {
                "kind": "string"
              },
              "default": "",

              "description": "Production function whose rate, with the equilibrium, sets how long small craters last.",
              "unit": "",
              "schema": {
                "kind": "enum",
                "choices": [
                  "neukum",
                  "extended_neukum",
                  "ivanov"
                ],
                "descriptions": [
                  "Neukum et al. (2001) lunar production function, valid from 10 m to 300 km.",
                  "The Neukum production function continued below 10 m as a power law of slope -2.85, valid from 2.5 m to 300 km.",
                  "Ivanov (2001) Martian production function, valid from 15 m to 362 km."
                ]
              },
              "default": "extended_neukum"
            },
            {
              "name": "equilibrium",
              "description": "Equilibrium density that, with the production rate, sets how long small craters last before they are erased.",
              "unit": "",
              "schema": {
                "kind": "enum",
                "choices": [
                  "trask",
                  "hartmann"
                ],
                "descriptions": [
                  "Trask (1966) lunar equilibrium, N(>=D) = 10^-1.1 D^-2, as the DSNE uses.",
                  "Hartmann (1984) lunar equilibrium, N(>=D) = 10^-1.14 D^-1.83 per km^2 with D in km."
                ]
              },
              "default": "hartmann"
            },
            {
              "name": "chronology",
              "description": "Chronology whose formation rate the craters' ages are drawn from.",
              "unit": "",
              "schema": {
                "kind": "enum",
                "choices": [
                  "neukum",
                  "ivanov"
                ],
                "descriptions": [
                  "Neukum et al. (2001) lunar chronology, for surfaces 0 to 4.6 Gyr old.",
                  "Ivanov (2001) Martian chronology, for surfaces 0 to 4.6 Gyr old."
                ]
              },
              "default": "neukum"
            }
          ],
          "default": {
            "type": "steady_state",
            "age_gyr": 3.5,
            "production": "extended_neukum",
            "equilibrium": "hartmann",
            "chronology": "neukum"
          }
        },
        {
          "type": "freshness",
          "description": "Ages from a freshness f between 0 and 1 drawn per crater, age = (1 - f) lifetime, with one lifetime for every diameter; freshness stands for age as in degree-of-freshness dating (Pohn and Offield 1970; Trang et al. 2015).",
          "fields": [
            {
              "name": "lifetime_gyr",

              "unit": "Gyr",

              },
              "default": 1.0,
              "minimum": 0.0,
              "exclusive_minimum": true
            },
            {
              "name": "freshness",
              "description": "Distribution each crater's freshness is drawn from, also clamped to 0 to 1: 1 is fresh, 0 at the end of its lifetime; with freshness degradation, depth and rim scale with it.",
              "unit": "",
              "schema": {

                "ref": "d11"
              },
              "default": {

              }
            }

          "default": 1.2,
          "minimum": 1.0,
          "exclusive_minimum": true
        },
        {
          "name": "shape",

            "kind": "enum",

              "linear",
              "smoothstep",
              "smootherstep",
              "gaussian"
            ],
            "descriptions": [
              "Straight ramp: continuous, with kinks at both ends.",
              "Cubic 3t^2 - 2t^3: continuous slope across the transition.",
              "Quintic 6t^5 - 15t^4 + 10t^3: continuous slope and curvature, the smoothest join.",
              "Gaussian falloff with sigma a third of the band, rescaled to end at zero."

          },
          "default": "smootherstep"
        },

    "d18": {

    "d29": {
      "kind": "object",
      "fields": [
        {
          "name": "path",
          "description": "GeoTIFF read in the surface's coordinates, relative to the configuration's folder: meters on a plane, longitude and latitude in degrees on a sphere. Empty uses value.",
          "unit": "",
          "schema": {
            "kind": "string"
          },
          "default": ""
        },
        {
          "name": "value",
          "description": "The field everywhere when no path is given.",
          "unit": "",
          "schema": {
            "kind": "number"
          },
          "default": 0.0
        },
        {
          "name": "band",
          "description": "Band of the GeoTIFF read, from 0.",
          "unit": "",
          "schema": {
            "kind": "integer",
            "minimum": 0
          },
          "default": 0
        },
        {
          "name": "method",
          "description": "How the raster is interpolated: nearest or bilinear, which stay within the cells read.",
          "unit": "",
          "schema": {
            "kind": "enum",
            "choices": [
              "nearest",
              "bilinear",
              "cubic",
              "catmull_rom",
              "lanczos3",
              "cubic_bspline"
            ],
            "descriptions": [
              "The value of the nearest cell center: blocky, but never mixes values.",
              "Linear in each axis over the four surrounding cells.",
              "Keys cubic convolution (a = -0.5) over the sixteen surrounding cells: smooth, for upscaling DEMs.",
              "Another name for cubic: the Catmull-Rom spline is the same kernel.",
              "The three-lobe Lanczos kernel over the 36 surrounding cells: sharper than cubic, with slight ringing at steps.",
              "The cubic B-spline over the sixteen surrounding cells: the smoothest, but it smooths the cells themselves."
            ]
          },
          "default": "bilinear"
        },
        {
          "name": "scale",
          "description": "Multiplies every cell, such as 0.001 for a map stored in thousandths. Must be positive.",
          "unit": "",
          "schema": {
            "kind": "number"
          },
          "default": 1.0,
          "minimum": 0.0,
          "exclusive_minimum": true
        },
        {
          "name": "fallback",
          "description": "Value outside the raster and where its cells are no-data or NaN; unset leaves none, and the layer then keeps its own setting there.",
          "unit": "",
          "schema": {
            "kind": "optional",
            "of": {
              "kind": "number"
            },
            "default": 0.0
          },
          "default": null
        },
        {
          "name": "periodic_longitude",
          "description": "The raster's x is longitude repeating every 360 degrees, so a map from 0 to 360 serves -180 to 180.",
          "unit": "",
          "schema": {
            "kind": "boolean"
          },
          "default": false
        }
      ]
    },

      "kind": "object",

          "exclusive_minimum": false
        },

        {

          "unit": "m^2",
          "schema": {

          },
          "default": 1.0,
          "minimum": 0.0,
          "exclusive_minimum": true

        {

          "unit": "",

          },
          "default": true

    "d30": {
      "kind": "object",

        {

          "unit": "",

Unset follows source_resolves_px; lower it to clean up the smaller craters a coarser run drew blurred into the source. Must be positive.",
          "unit": "px",

        {

              "kind": "number"
            },

    "d34": {

          "exclusive_maximum": false
        },
        {
          "name": "fracture_depth",
          "description": "Range of where each fracture plane lies, as a share of the shape's reach along its normal, within (0, 1]; lower values cut more away.",
          "unit": "",
          "schema": {
            "kind": "ref",
            "ref": "d43"
          },
          "default": {
            "min": 0.6,
            "max": 0.9
          }
        },
        {
          "name": "max_fracture_tilt",
          "description": "Largest vertical component of a fracture plane's unit normal: 0 keeps normals horizontal, cutting a slab about its rim only. Must be from 0 to 1.",
          "unit": "",
          "schema": {
            "kind": "number"
          },
          "default": 1.0,
          "minimum": 0.0,
          "exclusive_minimum": false,
          "maximum": 1.0,
          "exclusive_maximum": false
        },
        {
          "name": "noise_amplitude",
          "description": "Largest relative change of the radius by the roughening noise; 0 leaves the surface unroughened. Must be from 0 to below 1.",
          "unit": "",
          "schema": {
            "kind": "number"
          },
          "default": 0.05,
          "minimum": 0.0,
          "exclusive_minimum": false,
          "maximum": 1.0,
          "exclusive_maximum": true
        },
        {
          "name": "noise_wavelength",
          "description": "Wavelength of the roughening noise's first octave, in long-axis lengths; smaller values give finer bumps. Must be positive.",
          "unit": "",
          "schema": {
            "kind": "number"
          },
          "default": 0.6,
          "minimum": 0.0,
          "exclusive_minimum": true
        },
        {
          "name": "noise_octaves",
          "description": "Octaves of the roughening noise, each halving in wavelength; more add finer detail. Must be from 1 to 12.",
          "unit": "",
          "schema": {
            "kind": "integer"
          },
          "default": 3,
          "minimum": 1.0,
          "exclusive_minimum": false,
          "maximum": 12.0,
          "exclusive_maximum": false
        },
        {
          "name": "edge_softness",
          "description": "Range of how far edges and corners are worn back where faces meet, as weathering rounds them, in long-axis lengths from 0 to 0.5; 0 keeps them sharp.",
          "unit": "",
          "schema": {
            "kind": "ref",
            "ref": "d43"
          },
          "default": {
            "min": 0.0,
            "max": 0.0
          }
        },
        {
          "name": "face_roughness",
          "description": "How far fracture faces undulate, as a share of each plane's offset; 0 keeps them flat. Must be from 0 to 0.5.",
          "unit": "",
          "schema": {
            "kind": "number"
          },
          "default": 0.0,
          "minimum": 0.0,
          "exclusive_minimum": false,
          "maximum": 0.5,
          "exclusive_maximum": false
        }
      ]
    },

    "d44": {
      "kind": "object",
      "fields": [
        {
          "name": "field",
          "description": "The map.",
          "unit": "",
          "schema": {
            "kind": "ref",
            "ref": "d29"
          },
          "default": {
            "path": "",
            "value": 0.0,
            "band": 0,
            "method": "bilinear",
            "scale": 1.0,
            "fallback": null,
            "periodic_longitude": false
          }
        },
        {
          "name": "measure",
          "description": "What the map's values measure.",
          "unit": "",
          "schema": {
            "kind": "enum",
            "choices": [
              "exponent",
              "mean_diameter"
            ],
            "descriptions": [
              "The cumulative exponent alpha, counts falling as D^-alpha.",
              "The mean diameter in meters of the features from the reference diameter up, from which alpha = mean / (mean - D0)."
            ]
          },
          "default": "exponent"
        },
        {
          "name": "reference_diameter_m",
          "description": "Diameter D0 in meters where the local power law meets the layer's own count, as N(>=D) = N(>=D0) (D / D0)^-alpha; for a mean diameter map, the smallest diameter averaged. Must be positive.",
          "unit": "m",
          "schema": {
            "kind": "number"
          },
          "default": 1.0,
          "minimum": 0.0,
          "exclusive_minimum": true
        },
        {
          "name": "min_exponent",
          "description": "Smallest exponent alpha the map's values are clamped to; with the largest it bounds the boulders drawn, so generous bounds draw more to thin. Must be positive.",
          "unit": "",
          "schema": {
            "kind": "number"
          },
          "default": 1.0,
          "minimum": 0.0,
          "exclusive_minimum": true
        },
        {
          "name": "max_exponent",
          "description": "Largest exponent alpha the map's values are clamped to; above the smallest. Must be positive.",
          "unit": "",
          "schema": {
            "kind": "number"
          },
          "default": 6.0,
          "minimum": 0.0,
          "exclusive_minimum": true
        }
      ]
    },
    "d45": {
      "kind": "object",
      "fields": [
        {
          "name": "x",
          "description": "Center along x in the surface's coordinates; the longitude in degrees on a sphere.",
          "unit": "",
          "schema": {
            "kind": "number"
          },
          "default": 0.0
        },
        {
          "name": "y",
          "description": "Center along y in the surface's coordinates; the latitude in degrees on a sphere.",
          "unit": "",
          "schema": {
            "kind": "number"
          },
          "default": 0.0
        },
        {
          "name": "diameter_m",
          "description": "Length of the long axis, in meters. Must be positive.",
          "unit": "m",
          "schema": {
            "kind": "number"
          },
          "default": 0.0,
          "minimum": 0.0,
          "exclusive_minimum": true
        },
        {
          "name": "id",
          "description": "Stable ID that seeds what is drawn for the boulder; unset derives one from its position and diameter.",
          "unit": "",
          "schema": {
            "kind": "optional",
            "of": {
              "kind": "integer",
              "minimum": 0
            },
            "default": 0
          },
          "default": null
        },
        {
          "name": "height_m",
          "description": "Vertical extent in meters, buried part included; unset draws it from the height ratios. Must be positive.",
          "unit": "m",
          "schema": {
            "kind": "optional",
            "of": {
              "kind": "number"
            },
            "default": 0.0
          },
          "default": null,
          "minimum": 0.0,
          "exclusive_minimum": true
        },
        {
          "name": "burial",
          "description": "Buried share of the height; unset draws it. Must be from 0 to below 1.",
          "unit": "",
          "schema": {
            "kind": "optional",
            "of": {
              "kind": "number"
            },
            "default": 0.0
          },
          "default": null,
          "minimum": 0.0,
          "exclusive_minimum": false,
          "maximum": 1.0,
          "exclusive_maximum": true
        },
        {
          "name": "yaw_deg",
          "description": "Rotation about the vertical, degrees counter-clockwise from east; unset draws it.",
          "unit": "deg",
          "schema": {
            "kind": "optional",
            "of": {
              "kind": "number"
            },
            "default": 0.0
          },
          "default": null
        },
        {
          "name": "lean_deg",
          "description": "Tilt of the boulder's vertical axis from the vertical, degrees; unset draws it.",
          "unit": "deg",
          "schema": {
            "kind": "optional",
            "of": {
              "kind": "number"
            },
            "default": 0.0
          },
          "default": null
        },
        {
          "name": "tilt_deg",
          "description": "Angle of the up axis from the vertical after lean, degrees; unset draws it. A followed slope tips it further.",
          "unit": "deg",
          "schema": {
            "kind": "optional",
            "of": {
              "kind": "number"
            },
            "default": 0.0
          },
          "default": null
        },
        {
          "name": "tilt_azimuth_deg",
          "description": "Direction the up axis tips toward, degrees counter-clockwise from east; unset draws it.",
          "unit": "deg",
          "schema": {
            "kind": "optional",
            "of": {
              "kind": "number"
            },
            "default": 0.0
          },
          "default": null
        },
        {
          "name": "wear",
          "description": "How worn it is, 0 fresh; unset draws it. With burial_by_wear it sets a drawn burial. Must be from 0 to 1.",
          "unit": "",
          "schema": {
            "kind": "optional",
            "of": {
              "kind": "number"
            },
            "default": 0.0
          },
          "default": null,
          "minimum": 0.0,
          "exclusive_minimum": false,
          "maximum": 1.0,
          "exclusive_maximum": false
        },
        {
          "name": "model",
          "description": "Whether it is a 3D model rather than relief in the heights; unset follows the layer's model threshold.",
          "unit": "",
          "schema": {
            "kind": "optional",
            "of": {
              "kind": "boolean"
            },
            "default": false
          },
          "default": null
        },
        {
          "name": "rest",
          "description": "Which axis it stands along; unset draws it. A fixed lean, tilt, tilt azimuth or rest keeps a model from being tipped over by settle.",
          "unit": "",
          "schema": {
            "kind": "optional",
            "of": {
              "kind": "enum",
              "choices": [
                "face",
                "side",
                "end"
              ],
              "descriptions": [
                "On its broadest face: its short axis up.",
                "On a side: its intermediate axis up.",
                "On an end: its long axis up."
              ]
            },
            "default": "face"
          },
          "default": null
        },
        {
          "name": "shape_seed",
          "description": "Seed of its 3D shape, as a generated boulder's derived one; unset derives it from the ID.",
          "unit": "",
          "schema": {
            "kind": "optional",
            "of": {
              "kind": "integer",
              "minimum": 0
            },
            "default": 0
          },
          "default": null
        }
      ]
    },

      "kind": "choice",

        {

                "kind": "array",
                "of": {
                  "kind": "array",

    "d50": {
      "kind": "object",
      "fields": [
        {
          "name": "wavelength_m",

          "unit": "m",

          "minimum": 0.0,
          "exclusive_minimum": true

        {

            "kind": "number"
          },
          "default": 0.2,
          "minimum": 0.0,
          "exclusive_minimum": false
        },
        {
          "name": "lee_fraction",
          "description": "Share of a ripple wavelength the lee face takes: 0.5 is symmetric, lower values give a steeper lee face. Must be above 0 and below 1.",
          "unit": "",
          "schema": {
            "kind": "number"
          },
          "default": 0.5,
          "minimum": 0.0,
          "exclusive_minimum": true,
          "maximum": 1.0,
          "exclusive_maximum": true
        },
        {
          "name": "sinuosity",
          "description": "How far a ripple crest wanders along its length, in wavelengths. Must not be negative.",
          "unit": "",
          "schema": {
            "kind": "number"
          },
          "default": 0.3,
          "minimum": 0.0,
          "exclusive_minimum": false
        },
        {
          "name": "slope_coupling",
          "description": "How strongly the dune's slope turns and tightens the ripples: they shorten on steep lee faces and turn on the flanks; 0 keeps them straight across the wind. Must not be negative.",
          "unit": "",
          "schema": {
            "kind": "number"
          },
          "default": 1.0,
          "minimum": 0.0,
          "exclusive_minimum": false
        },
        {
          "name": "interdune_cover",
          "description": "Share of the ripple height kept on the ground between dunes. Must be from 0 to 1.",
          "unit": "",
          "schema": {
            "kind": "number"
          },
          "default": 0.0,
          "minimum": 0.0,
          "exclusive_minimum": false,
          "maximum": 1.0,
          "exclusive_maximum": false
        },
        {
          "name": "defect_density",
          "description": "Forked crests (Y-junctions): pairs of crest ends per meter of crest, as measured on dune fields (Ewing et al. 2010); 0 for none. Mars large ripples: 0.099. Must not be negative.",
          "unit": "1/m",
          "schema": {
            "kind": "number"
          },
          "default": 0.0,
          "minimum": 0.0,
          "exclusive_minimum": false
        },
        {
          "name": "flank_straightening",
          "description": "How far crests straighten off the stoss: 1 keeps the sinuosity on flat sand and stoss slopes and takes it away on flanks and lee slopes, as Martian large ripples do. Must be from 0 to 1.",
          "unit": "",
          "schema": {
            "kind": "number"
          },
          "default": 0.0,
          "minimum": 0.0,
          "exclusive_minimum": false,
          "maximum": 1.0,
          "exclusive_maximum": false
        },
        {
          "name": "fade_px",
          "description": "How ripples too fine for the sample spacing fade out, by samples per wavelength. Each must not be negative.",
          "unit": "px",
          "schema": {
            "kind": "array",
            "of": {
              "kind": "number"
            },
            "default": 0.0,
            "length": 2
          },
          "default": [
            2.0,
            4.0
          ],
          "minimum": 0.0,
          "exclusive_minimum": false
        },
        {
          "name": "fade_shape",
          "description": "Curve of the fade between the two sample counts of fade_px.",
          "unit": "",
          "schema": {
            "kind": "enum",
            "choices": [
              "linear",
              "smoothstep",
              "smootherstep",
              "gaussian"
            ],
            "descriptions": [
              "Straight ramp: continuous, with kinks at both ends.",
              "Cubic 3t^2 - 2t^3: continuous slope across the transition.",
              "Quintic 6t^5 - 15t^4 + 10t^3: continuous slope and curvature, the smoothest join.",
              "Gaussian falloff with sigma a third of the band, rescaled to end at zero."
            ]
          },
          "default": "smoothstep"
        }
      ]
    },

          "type": "boulders",
          "description": "Boulders scattered over the ground from a size distribution, in patches and around fresh craters, as relief or 3D models.",
          "fields": [
            {
              "name": "generate_random",
              "description": "Draws random boulders from the size distribution, between craters and around them; off places only the manual boulders, and the sizes, coverage and ejecta go unused.",
              "unit": "",
              "schema": {
                "kind": "boolean"
              },
              "default": true
            },
            {
              "name": "coverage",
              "description": "Golombek-Rapp k, the fraction of the ground covered by boulders, above 0 when generating random boulders; higher values give more boulders. Unset is 0.02. Only golombek_rapp sizes use it, so set it only with them. Must be from 0 to below 1.",
              "unit": "",
              "schema": {
                "kind": "optional",
                "of": {
                  "kind": "number"
                },
                "default": 0.0
              },
              "default": null,
              "minimum": 0.0,
              "exclusive_minimum": false,
              "maximum": 1.0,
              "exclusive_maximum": true
            },
            {
              "name": "qa",
              "description": "Constant term of the Golombek-Rapp q = qa + qb / k, per meter; a larger q leaves fewer large boulders. Unset is 1.79. Only golombek_rapp sizes or ejecta sizes use it, so set it only with them.",
              "unit": "1/m",
              "schema": {
                "kind": "optional",
                "of": {
                  "kind": "number"
                },
                "default": 0.0
              },
              "default": null
            },
            {
              "name": "qb",
              "description": "Term of the Golombek-Rapp q = qa + qb / k divided by the coverage k, per meter; unset is 0.152, and it is used as qa is.",
              "unit": "1/m",
              "schema": {
                "kind": "optional",
                "of": {
                  "kind": "number"
                },
                "default": 0.0
              },
              "default": null

    "d56": {
      "kind": "object",
      "fields": [
        {
          "name": "enabled",
          "description": "Includes this layer in the stack; disabled layers are skipped.",
          "unit": "",
          "schema": {
            "kind": "boolean"
          },
          "default": true
        },
        {
          "name": "basis",
          "description": "Single-octave noise the fractal is built from.",
          "unit": "",
          "schema": {
            "kind": "enum",
            "choices": [
              "perlin",
              "simplex",
              "value",
              "worley_f1",
              "worley_f2",
              "worley_f2_minus_f1",
              "voronoi"
            ],
            "descriptions": [
              "Improved Perlin gradient noise: smooth, general-purpose relief.",
              "Simplex gradient noise: smooth relief, an alternative to Perlin.",
              "Value noise: random values interpolated over a lattice; blockier than gradient noise.",
              "Cellular noise from the distance to the nearest feature point: cones and basins.",
              "Cellular noise from the distance to the second-nearest feature point.",
              "Cellular noise F2 - F1: ridges along cell borders, like cracked ground.",
              "Voronoi cells, each at one random height: flat polygonal plateaus and terraces."
            ]
          },
          "default": "perlin"
        },
        {
          "name": "fractal",
          "description": "How the octaves of the basis noise are combined.",
          "unit": "",
          "schema": {
            "kind": "enum",
            "choices": [
              "fbm",
              "ridged",
              "billow",
              "hybrid_multifractal"
            ],
            "descriptions": [
              "Fractional Brownian motion: a weighted sum of octaves, the general-purpose choice.",
              "Ridged multifractal: sharp crests from inverted absolute noise, like eroded ridges.",
              "Sum of absolute-value octaves: rounded, puffy forms.",
              "Hybrid multifractal: smooth lowlands and rough highlands."
            ]
          },
          "default": "fbm"
        },
        {
          "name": "blend",
          "description": "How this layer combines with the height of the layers before it; the first enabled layer sets the height instead.",
          "unit": "",
          "schema": {
            "kind": "enum",
            "choices": [
              "add",
              "max",
              "min",
              "mask"
            ],
            "descriptions": [
              "Adds the layer to the height so far.",
              "Keeps the higher of the height so far and the layer.",
              "Keeps the lower of the height so far and the layer.",
              "Multiplies the height so far by (layer / amplitude + 1) / 2, so the layer modulates roughness by region."
            ]
          },
          "default": "add"
        },
        {
          "name": "seed",
          "description": "Seed of the noise; changing it gives a different pattern of the same character.",
          "unit": "",
          "schema": {
            "kind": "integer",
            "minimum": 0
          },
          "default": 0
        },
        {
          "name": "wavelength_m",
          "description": "Wavelength of the first, broadest octave, in meters; sets the size of the largest features. Must be positive.",
          "unit": "m",
          "schema": {
            "kind": "number"
          },
          "default": 1000.0,
          "minimum": 0.0,
          "exclusive_minimum": true
        },
        {
          "name": "amplitude",
          "description": "Largest value of the layer above or below 0, in what its stack varies: relative brightness, saturation or degrees of hue. Required.",
          "unit": "",
          "schema": {
            "kind": "optional",
            "of": {
              "kind": "number"
            },
            "default": 0.0
          },
          "default": null,
          "required": true
        },
        {
          "name": "octaves",
          "description": "Number of octaves; each one adds detail at a shorter wavelength. Must be from 1 to 32.",
          "unit": "",
          "schema": {
            "kind": "integer"
          },
          "default": 8,
          "minimum": 1.0,
          "exclusive_minimum": false,
          "maximum": 32.0,
          "exclusive_maximum": false
        },
        {
          "name": "lacunarity",
          "description": "Frequency ratio between successive octaves. Must be above 1.",
          "unit": "",
          "schema": {
            "kind": "number"
          },
          "default": 2.0,
          "minimum": 1.0,
          "exclusive_minimum": true
        },
        {
          "name": "gain",
          "description": "Weight ratio between successive octaves; higher values give rougher terrain. Unused when the Hurst exponent is set. Must be positive.",
          "unit": "",
          "schema": {
            "kind": "number"
          },
          "default": 0.5,
          "minimum": 0.0,
          "exclusive_minimum": true
        },
        {
          "name": "hurst",
          "description": "Hurst exponent that sets the octave gain to lacunarity^-hurst: near 1 is smooth, lower is rougher at short baselines. Unset uses the gain.",
          "unit": "",
          "schema": {
            "kind": "optional",
            "of": {
              "kind": "number"
            },
            "default": 0.0
          },
          "default": null
        },
        {
          "name": "offset",
          "description": "Ridge offset of the ridged and hybrid multifractal types. Must be positive.",
          "unit": "",
          "schema": {
            "kind": "number"
          },
          "default": 1.0,
          "minimum": 0.0,
          "exclusive_minimum": true
        },
        {
          "name": "warp_amplitude_m",
          "description": "Domain warp displacement in meters, which bends the noise into swirled shapes; 0 disables warping. Must not be negative.",
          "unit": "m",
          "schema": {
            "kind": "number"
          },
          "default": 0.0,
          "minimum": 0.0,
          "exclusive_minimum": false
        },
        {
          "name": "warp_wavelength_m",
          "description": "Wavelength of the warp field, in meters. Must be positive.",
          "unit": "m",
          "schema": {
            "kind": "number"
          },
          "default": 500.0,
          "minimum": 0.0,
          "exclusive_minimum": true
        }
      ]
    },
    "d57": {
      "kind": "object",
      "fields": [
        {
          "name": "enabled",
          "description": "Adds fractal detail below the map's resolution; off leaves the interpolated map as it is.",
          "unit": "",
          "schema": {
            "kind": "boolean"
          },
          "default": true
        },
        {
          "name": "seed",
          "description": "Seed of the detail noise; changing it gives a different pattern of the same roughness.",
          "unit": "",
          "schema": {
            "kind": "integer",
            "minimum": 0
          },
          "default": 0
        },
        {
          "name": "octaves",
          "description": "Octaves of detail, from half the map's cell size down, each half the wavelength of the one before. Must be from 1 to 16.",
          "unit": "",
          "schema": {
            "kind": "integer"
          },
          "default": 4,
          "minimum": 1.0,
          "exclusive_minimum": false,
          "maximum": 16.0,
          "exclusive_maximum": false
        },
        {
          "name": "scale",
          "description": "Factor on the RMS of every octave; 0 adds no detail, higher values give a more mottled albedo. Must not be negative.",
          "unit": "",
          "schema": {
            "kind": "number"
          },
          "default": 1.0,
          "minimum": 0.0,
          "exclusive_minimum": false
        },
        {
          "name": "hurst",
          "description": "Hurst exponent used instead of the one measured from the map; lower values keep more contrast at fine scales. Unset uses the measured one. Must be from 0 to 1.",
          "unit": "",
          "schema": {
            "kind": "optional",
            "of": {
              "kind": "number"
            },
            "default": 0.0
          },
          "default": null,
          "minimum": 0.0,
          "exclusive_minimum": false,
          "maximum": 1.0,
          "exclusive_maximum": false
        },
        {
          "name": "fade_px",
          "description": "How octaves of detail too fine for the sample spacing fade out. Each must not be negative.",
          "unit": "px",
          "schema": {
            "kind": "array",
            "of": {
              "kind": "number"
            },
            "default": 0.0,
            "length": 2
          },
          "default": [
            2.0,
            4.0
          ],
          "minimum": 0.0,
          "exclusive_minimum": false
        },
        {
          "name": "fade_shape",
          "description": "Curve of the fade between the two sample counts of fade_px.",
          "unit": "",
          "schema": {
            "kind": "enum",
            "choices": [
              "linear",
              "smoothstep",
              "smootherstep",
              "gaussian"
            ],
            "descriptions": [
              "Straight ramp: continuous, with kinks at both ends.",
              "Cubic 3t^2 - 2t^3: continuous slope across the transition.",
              "Quintic 6t^5 - 15t^4 + 10t^3: continuous slope and curvature, the smoothest join.",
              "Gaussian falloff with sigma a third of the band, rescaled to end at zero."
            ]
          },
          "default": "smoothstep"
        }
      ]
    },
    "d55": {
      "kind": "choice",
      "alternatives": [
        {
          "type": "synthetic",
          "description": "A base color in hue, saturation and value, each varied by noise: an albedo for terrain without data.",
          "fields": [
            {
              "name": "rgb",
              "description": "Gives three bands, red, green and blue, from the color; off gives one band of the value alone, ignoring hue and saturation.",
              "unit": "",
              "schema": {
                "kind": "boolean"
              },
              "default": false
            },
            {
              "name": "hue_deg",
              "description": "Hue of the base color in degrees, wrapping around; used with rgb only.",
              "unit": "deg",
              "schema": {
                "kind": "number"
              },
              "default": 0.0
            },
            {
              "name": "saturation",
              "description": "Saturation of the base color, 0 for gray; used with rgb only. Must be from 0 to 1.",
              "unit": "",
              "schema": {
                "kind": "number"
              },
              "default": 0.0,
              "minimum": 0.0,
              "exclusive_minimum": false,
              "maximum": 1.0,
              "exclusive_maximum": false
            },
            {
              "name": "value",
              "description": "Reflectance of the brightest band; the one band's value without rgb. Higher values give a brighter surface. Must be from 0 to 1.",
              "unit": "",
              "schema": {
                "kind": "number"
              },
              "default": 0.11,
              "minimum": 0.0,
              "exclusive_minimum": false,
              "maximum": 1.0,
              "exclusive_maximum": false
            },
            {
              "name": "hue_noise_deg",
              "description": "Noise layers whose sum in degrees is added to the hue; used with rgb only. Holds 0 to 8 items.",
              "unit": "",
              "schema": {
                "kind": "array",
                "of": {
                  "kind": "ref",

                  "seed": 0,
                  "wavelength_m": 1000.0,
                  "amplitude": null,

                  "gain": 0.5,
                  "hurst": null,
                  "offset": 1.0,
                  "warp_amplitude_m": 0.0,
                  "warp_wavelength_m": 500.0
                }
              },
              "default": [],
              "min_length": 0,
              "max_length": 8
            },
            {
              "name": "saturation_noise",
              "description": "Noise layers added to the saturation, which is then clamped to [0, 1]; used with rgb only. Holds 0 to 8 items.",
              "unit": "",
              "schema": {
                "kind": "array",
                "of": {
                  "kind": "ref",
                  "ref": "d56"
                },
                "default": {
                  "enabled": true,
                  "basis": "perlin",
                  "fractal": "fbm",
                  "blend": "add",
                  "seed": 0,
                  "wavelength_m": 1000.0,
                  "amplitude": null,
                  "octaves": 8,
                  "lacunarity": 2.0,
                  "gain": 0.5,
                  "hurst": null,
                  "offset": 1.0,
                  "warp_amplitude_m": 0.0,
                  "warp_wavelength_m": 500.0
                }
              },
              "default": [],
              "min_length": 0,
              "max_length": 8
            },
            {
              "name": "value_noise",
              "description": "Noise layers: the value is multiplied by 1 plus their sum and clamped to [0, 1], so their amplitude sets the relative contrast. Holds 0 to 8 items.",
              "unit": "",
              "schema": {
                "kind": "array",
                "of": {
                  "kind": "ref",
                  "ref": "d56"
                },
                "default": {
                  "enabled": true,
                  "basis": "perlin",
                  "fractal": "fbm",
                  "blend": "add",
                  "seed": 0,
                  "wavelength_m": 1000.0,
                  "amplitude": null,
                  "octaves": 8,
                  "lacunarity": 2.0,
                  "gain": 0.5,
                  "hurst": null,
                  "offset": 1.0,
                  "warp_amplitude_m": 0.0,
                  "warp_wavelength_m": 500.0
                }
              },
              "default": [],
              "min_length": 0,
              "max_length": 8
            }
          ],
          "default": {
            "type": "synthetic",
            "rgb": false,
            "hue_deg": 0.0,
            "saturation": 0.0,
            "value": 0.11,
            "hue_noise_deg": [],
            "saturation_noise": [],
            "value_noise": []
          }
        },
        {
          "type": "raster",
          "description": "Albedo read from one or three bands of a GeoTIFF in the terrain's projection, such as an orbital albedo map.",
          "fields": [
            {
              "name": "path",
              "description": "GeoTIFF albedo map in the terrain's projected coordinates; relative paths resolve against the configuration's folder. Required.",
              "unit": "",
              "schema": {
                "kind": "string"
              },
              "default": "",
              "required": true
            },
            {
              "name": "bands",
              "description": "Bands of the file to read, counting from 0: one for a single albedo band, or three for red, green and blue. Holds 1 or 3 items.",
              "unit": "",
              "schema": {
                "kind": "array",
                "of": {
                  "kind": "integer",
                  "minimum": 0
                },
                "default": 0
              },
              "default": [
                0
              ],
              "lengths": [
                1,
                3
              ]
            },
            {
              "name": "scale",
              "description": "Factor each sample is multiplied by, replacing the band's scale from the file's GDAL metadata, as for maps stored as integers. Unset keeps the file's.",
              "unit": "",
              "schema": {
                "kind": "optional",
                "of": {
                  "kind": "number"
                },
                "default": 0.0
              },
              "default": null
            },
            {
              "name": "offset",
              "description": "Added to each scaled sample, replacing the band's offset from the file's GDAL metadata. Unset keeps the file's.",
              "unit": "",
              "schema": {
                "kind": "optional",
                "of": {
                  "kind": "number"
                },
                "default": 0.0
              },
              "default": null
            },
            {
              "name": "resampling",
              "description": "Interpolation used to sample the map at the terrain's points.",
              "unit": "",
              "schema": {
                "kind": "enum",
                "choices": [
                  "nearest",
                  "bilinear",
                  "cubic",
                  "catmull_rom",
                  "lanczos3",
                  "cubic_bspline"
                ],
                "descriptions": [
                  "The value of the nearest cell center: blocky, but never mixes values.",
                  "Linear in each axis over the four surrounding cells.",
                  "Keys cubic convolution (a = -0.5) over the sixteen surrounding cells: smooth, for upscaling DEMs.",
                  "Another name for cubic: the Catmull-Rom spline is the same kernel.",
                  "The three-lobe Lanczos kernel over the 36 surrounding cells: sharper than cubic, with slight ringing at steps.",
                  "The cubic B-spline over the sixteen surrounding cells: the smoothest, but it smooths the cells themselves."
                ]
              },
              "default": "cubic"
            },
            {
              "name": "detail",
              "description": "Fractal detail below the map's resolution, continuing the map's own measured roughness to finer scales.",
              "unit": "",
              "schema": {
                "kind": "ref",
                "ref": "d57"
              },
              "default": {
                "enabled": true,
                "seed": 0,
                "octaves": 4,
                "scale": 1.0,
                "hurst": null,
                "fade_px": [
                  2.0,
                  4.0
                ],
                "fade_shape": "smoothstep"
              }
            }
          ],
          "default": {
            "type": "raster",
            "path": "",
            "bands": [
              0
            ],
            "scale": null,
            "offset": null,
            "resampling": "cubic",
            "detail": {
              "enabled": true,
              "seed": 0,
              "octaves": 4,
              "scale": 1.0,
              "hurst": null,
              "fade_px": [
                2.0,
                4.0
              ],

            }
          }
        }
      ]

    "d59": {
      "kind": "object",

          "unit": "",

            "kind": "number"

          "exclusive_minimum": true
        },

          },

          "exclusive_minimum": true

          "exclusive_minimum": false
        },

          "maximum": 64.0,
          "exclusive_maximum": false
        },
        {

          "unit": "",

        {

    "d64": {
      "kind": "object",
      "fields": [
        {
          "name": "enabled",
          "description": "Draws an impact angle and direction per crater that shape its rays; off treats every impact as vertical.",
          "unit": "",
          "schema": {
            "kind": "boolean"
          },
          "default": true
        },
        {
          "name": "heading_deg",
          "description": "Downrange direction of every impact, in degrees counter-clockwise from +x (local east on a body); unset draws a random heading per crater.",
          "unit": "deg",
          "schema": {
            "kind": "optional",
            "of": {
              "kind": "number"
            },
            "default": 0.0
          },
          "default": null
        },
        {
          "name": "asymmetric_deg",
          "description": "Impact angle from the horizontal, in degrees, below which ejecta leave faster downrange, lengthening rays there and shortening them uprange. Must be from 0 to 90 deg.",
          "unit": "deg",
          "schema": {
            "kind": "number"
          },
          "default": 45.0,
          "minimum": 0.0,
          "exclusive_minimum": false,
          "maximum": 90.0,
          "exclusive_maximum": false
        },
        {
          "name": "forbidden_deg",
          "description": "Impact angle in degrees below which rays within the zone half width of uprange are dropped; at most the asymmetric angle. Must be from 0 to 90 deg.",
          "unit": "deg",
          "schema": {
            "kind": "number"
          },
          "default": 25.0,
          "minimum": 0.0,
          "exclusive_minimum": false,
          "maximum": 90.0,
          "exclusive_maximum": false
        },
        {
          "name": "butterfly_deg",
          "description": "Impact angle in degrees below which rays within the zone half width of downrange are dropped too, a butterfly pattern; at most the forbidden angle. Must be from 0 to 90 deg.",
          "unit": "deg",
          "schema": {
            "kind": "number"
          },
          "default": 10.0,
          "minimum": 0.0,
          "exclusive_minimum": false,
          "maximum": 90.0,
          "exclusive_maximum": false
        },
        {
          "name": "downrange_speed_ratio",
          "description": "Downrange over uprange ejection speed below the asymmetric angle, drawn per crater; at least 1, higher values stretch downrange rays more.",
          "unit": "",
          "schema": {
            "kind": "ref",
            "ref": "d11"
          },
          "default": {
            "kind": "uniform",
            "a": 1.2,
            "b": 1.4,
            "min": null,
            "max": null,
            "edges": [],
            "weights": []
          }
        },
        {
          "name": "zone_half_width_deg",
          "description": "Half width in degrees of the ray-free zones uprange and downrange; illustrative, as the sources do not measure it. Must be from 0 to 180 deg.",
          "unit": "deg",
          "schema": {
            "kind": "number"
          },
          "default": 45.0,
          "minimum": 0.0,
          "exclusive_minimum": false,
          "maximum": 180.0,
          "exclusive_maximum": false
        }
      ]

        },
